children: Copper prices are lower in early Asian trade, with a stronger dollar and rising LME inventories weighing on sentiment, says Changjiang Futures analysts in a note. However, losses may be limited by a rebound in overnight futures and declining inventories on the Shanghai Futures Exchange, they say. Copper is likely to continue consolidating, they add. The three-month LME copper contract is down 0.6% at $13,732.00 a ton. (jiahui.huang@wsj.com; @ivy_jiahuihuang)
